backtest_summary.dedupe_explanation: Repeated scheduled AWS scans are counted once per target, market, and side, using the first approved (entry) snapshot so approved metrics reflect trades actually taken, not the decayed last scan. Scanning runs both sides of each binary market, so the YES and NO snapshots of one market are then collapsed to a single scored observation (the model's favoured side) before Brier, log loss, hit rate and average probability are computed. Approved P&L still counts every approved snapshot. Figures published before 2026-08-07 scored both halves, which held hit rate and average probability near 0.50 and doubled the reported sample size; Brier and log loss are unchanged by the collapse.

release.comparison_note: v7 starts a separate paper research ledger. v6 losses, fills, goals and unsettled positions retain their original account and policy. No v6 result is counted as v7 performance.

findings.impact: The October 5 baseline still ran the September 4 backend; later sizing, partial-loss memory, execution and market coverage fixes were absent.
findings.state: baseline release gap; cutover verified separately
findings.title: Tested changes did not reach production

findings.impact: v6 filled 5,312.96 of 108,965 requested contracts (4.88%). Larger requests reserve capital without proving more liquidity or profit.
findings.title: Requested size is not filled size

findings.impact: v6 netted $17.93 on $3,927.86 resolved entry capital. Atlanta contributed -$123.98. A 72% trading win rate did not establish useful net returns.
findings.title: Losses erased most research gains

findings.impact: The preserved September journal review documented six incorrectly vetoed stop attempts after a partial exit. Dollar-loss guards must retain earlier realized slices across monitor restarts; saved dollars are not established.
findings.title: Partial exits lost earlier loss memory

findings.impact: A partial hourly response could masquerade as a whole-day high; duplicate source rows could overwrite one another. Neither defect is proven to explain the measured losses.
findings.state: v7 rejects incomplete input and separates sources
findings.title: Incomplete and mixed forecast inputs

findings.impact: Legacy duplicate lots could reuse one bid's liquidity, and execution-time timestamps concealed request age. V7 conserves each account's exit depth and retains the conservative request-start clock. Historical dollar impact remains unproven.
findings.state: v7 shares depth and preserves quote time
findings.title: Paper exits overstated quote evidence

findings.impact: Live and Research orders pooled finite tape despite separate ledgers. V7 gives each account an independent paper scenario while conserving volume across its own orders and restarts. Old results retain their original execution generation.
findings.state: v7 isolates economic accounts under exec-v5
findings.title: Separate experiments consumed each other's maker tape

findings.impact: Two diagnostics selected sigma from the realized temperature cohort. V7 selects it from the prediction, reports own-sigma postprocessor Brier separately, and labels retrospective diagnostics as in-sample rather than promotion evidence.
findings.title: Diagnostic uncertainty depended on the observed answer

findings.impact: Maker allocations, frozen goals and several research/settlement records were missing from nightly exports. V7 includes them and depth partitions, keeps all archived profiles visible, and starts immutable served forecast vintages without inventing historical inputs.
findings.state: v7 exports evidence and displays all eras
findings.title: Archives omitted important execution and research evidence

findings.impact: October 5 historical analysis still dated September 4. Reconstructed forecasts are not original decision-time runs. Full NO/maker replay and prospective calibration remain necessary before scaling.
findings.title: Old analysis and incomplete replay

findings.impact: Some EMOS, analog and cohort diagnostics used future truth relative to their serve date. V7 applies the lead cutoff and matches the challenger to production's 45-day bias-only correction. Retrospective weather skill remains separate from issued trading probabilities.
findings.state: v7 applies lead-aware truth cutoff and serving policy
findings.title: Backtests learned truth unavailable at serving

findings.impact: Dataset guidance could cross station or availability boundaries, and repeated vintages inflated MOS sample counts. V7 keeps station-days distinct, requires explicit approved keys and after-cost approval, and blocks automatic research promotion.
findings.state: v7 requires explicit after-cost approval and observed availability
findings.title: Accuracy scores were treated as live approval

findings.impact: A stale independent EMOS lookup could override the served forecast's distribution. V7 validates and uses the snapshot's own paired mean and sigma before applying intraday information.
findings.state: v7 couples mean and sigma before intraday adjustment
findings.title: Reports could pair probabilities with the wrong distribution

findings.evidence: reproduced signed and decimal boundary cases
findings.impact: A legacy label such as -5 or below could be interpreted as +5. V7 parses signed thresholds and explicit range separators. Old outcomes are not automatically rewritten; any restatement requires verified contract truth.
findings.state: v7 preserves signs and decimal ranges
findings.title: Legacy settlement labels lost negative signs
